key_points.point: Top-performing enterprises achieve massive output multiplication through intensive agentic AI adoption, as demonstrated by the widening productivity gap where frontier firms generate 8.3 times as many output tokens per active user as typical firms. The document measures this depth of use through administrative data showing that agentic workflows generate substantially more output by carrying out longer, multi-step tasks across enterprise customers. This expansion of output reflects the accelerationist thesis that advanced capabilities and tool-connected agents drive rapid efficiency gains and economic value creation across diverse industries. The document acknowledges that access alone is insufficient, noting that firms must also make complementary investments in data infrastructure and continuous learning to achieve these output multiples.
key_points.verbatim: Frontier firms—those in the top 10% of AI usage each month—now generate 8.3 × as many output tokens per active user as typical firms. The measure is a proxy for depth of use, and the widening gap appears alongside greater adoption of capabilities that connect agents to company context, tools, and repeatable workflows.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Frontier enterprises achieve massive output multiplication through intensive agentic AI adoption and tool integration.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that top-performing enterprises achieve massive output multiplication through intensive agentic AI adoption and tool integration, driving rapid operational efficiency. Encompasses: output token generation multiples, agentic workflow depth, enterprise productivity scaling.

key_points.point: Organizations should actively connect AI agents to company context and tools to transition enterprise workflows from mere assistance to autonomous execution. The document outlines how products like ChatGPT Work and Codex utilize plugins and skills to bundle reusable instructions with CRM data and internal codebases, enabling workers to delegate multi-step tasks such as drafting presentations or refactoring code. From an accelerationist perspective, embedding agents directly into operational workflows scales expert behaviors and accelerates productivity gains across knowledge-work functions. The document notes that realizing this potential requires establishing clear permissions and human review alongside automated execution.
key_points.verbatim: Together, the studies point to a practical enterprise agenda: connect agents to the context and tools needed to complete valuable work; establish clear permissions, review, and governance; and help employees turn effective individual workflows into shared ways of working.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Expand AI capabilities by connecting agents to company context and tools to transition from assistance to execution.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that expands AI capabilities by connecting agents to company context and tools to transition from assistance to execution. Encompasses: agentic workflow integration, tool-use enablement, enterprise productivity scaling.

key_points.point: Enterprise AI adoption is spreading rapidly across diverse knowledge-work functions, with weekly active Codex users growing significantly in legal, sales, recruiting, and marketing departments. The document supports this empirical claim with administrative usage data showing triple-digit growth in legal and double-digit growth in sales and recruiting, proving that agentic adoption extends far beyond software engineering. This widespread diffusion supports the accelerationist view that AI serves as a general-purpose technology driving net economic expansion and capability scaling across the entire enterprise economy. The document notes that engineering was merely an early center of adoption before these productivity multipliers generalized to all knowledge work.
key_points.verbatim: Since February, weekly active enterprise Codex users grew 108 % in legal, 41 % in sales, 41 % in recruiting, and 26 % in marketing, compared with 5 % in engineering.

key_points.point: Rapid enterprise adoption of agentic AI and advanced plugins requires establishing clear permissions, review, and governance to maintain institutional oversight. The document notes that as organizations transition from assistants to executing agents connected to company data and tools, governance frameworks must accompany technical deployment. From a safetyist perspective, scaling autonomous execution without robust visibility and control mechanisms risks operational blind spots and unauthorized data access. The document emphasizes that successful frontier firms combine deep tool integration with structured human review and governance protocols.

key_points.point: Early-career employees utilize AI at significantly higher rates than more senior executives, with early-career workers sending 13 more messages per week six months after adoption. The document substantiates this behavioral difference using administrative data from millions of conversations that contradicts popular survey claims of executive-led usage. From a skeptic perspective, this disparity indicates that AI integration is unevenly experienced and adopted across organizational hierarchies, potentially reflecting differing comparative advantages or pressures placed on junior staff. The document suggests leaders must study these grassroots employee workflows rather than assuming top-down executive usage drives transformation.
key_points.verbatim: Many surveys have reported higher levels of AI use among leaders and executives. However, administrative data from millions of conversations finds the opposite. Six months after adoption, early-career employees sent 13 more messages per week than executives.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Early-career employees use AI more, paragraphs 1-2
key_points.canonical_proposition: Early-career employees utilize AI at significantly higher rates than senior executives in enterprise settings.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that early-career employees utilize AI at significantly higher rates than senior executives in enterprise settings, revealing hierarchical disparities in workplace adoption. Encompasses: hierarchical adoption gaps, junior employee AI reliance, administrative usage tracking.

factual_claims.claim: Frontier firms in the top 10% of monthly AI usage generate 8.3 times as many output tokens per active user as typical firms, representing an increase from a 2.6 times gap in January.
As of June, Codex generated 64% of combined Codex and ChatGPT output tokens among enterprise customers, reflecting a shift toward agentic, multi-step tasks.
Weekly active users of enterprise Codex grew by 108% in legal, 41% in sales, 41% in recruiting, and 26% in marketing since February, compared to 5% in engineering.
Among weekly active users at frontier firms, 21% use plugins and 19% use skills, compared to 9% and 3% at typical firms, while internal OpenAI usage reaches 95% weekly plugin adoption.
Six months after enterprise adoption, early-career employees sent 13 more messages per week than executives, based on administrative data from millions of conversations.
